case.background: Monochromatic light passes through a homogeneous, dilute, noninteracting absorbing solution in its validated concentration range. Determine how transmitted power depends on incident power, solute concentration, and optical path length.
initial_observations: The solution does not fluoresce or scatter within the available range.

instruments.description: A monochromatic source, variable-power attenuator, calibrated solution cell with selectable path length, and transmitted-power detector.
instruments.name: solution_absorption_cell

notes: This is a deterministic idealized benchmark world, not a literal replay of a historical data table.
A valid experiment changes only listed controls and consumes one episode attempt.
The model uses the natural exponential (Napierian) convention. At the historical path exponent one, 0.6 mM^-1 corresponds to 0.6 mM^-1 cm^-1 before multiplying by the one-centimeter normalized path.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'expression'. FinalSubmission.parameters must equal {'outputs': {READOUT: EXPR, ...}} with exactly these readouts: transmitted_power_uw. EXPR is the shared family-neutral JSON arithmetic tree over public controls. Supported operators are: add, subtract, multiply, divide, power, negate, exp, log, sin, maximum, step. No candidate law family or truth-specific parameter slots are supplied.

readouts.description: Optical power leaving the solution cell.
readouts.name: transmitted_power_uw

case.title: Discover the optical attenuation relation

experiment.intent: Vary c and L at fixed P0 to distinguish exponential vs linear and check nonunit exponents.

hypotheses.statement: Transmitted power follows Beer-Lambert (Napierian): T = P0 * exp(-alpha * c * L) with alpha ~ 0.6 mM^-1 cm^-1.
Transmitted power decreases linearly in c*L: T = P0 * max(0, 1 - k*c*L) with k~0.6.
Nonunit exponents on c or L: T = P0*exp(-alpha*c^p*L^q) with p or q != 1.

Nonunit exponents on c or L: T = P0*exp(-alpha*c^p*L^q) with p or q != 1.
